transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm in the right place and not, you know, wasting your time. 

I guess I came in because... well, for the last few weeks, I’ve barely had an appetite. It's probably nothing too serious, but usually, after a long shift in the security room, I really look forward to eating. Lately, though, even the foods I usually like just sort of... sit there on the plate. I end up just forcing down a few bites so I don't run on empty. 

Is that... does that make sense to come in for? I just wanted to make sure I'm doing the right thing by getting it checked out.
Have you been feeling sad or down lately?

Well, I wouldn't say I'm sitting around crying or anything like that, so I don't want to make it sound worse than it is. But... yeah, I guess I have been feeling a bit down. 

Most days, I just feel like I'm carrying this... I don't know, this heavy, flat feeling around with me. It's hard to explain, but even when I'm home with my family, or just sitting in the break room at work, I feel like I'm just not really there. Like I'm just going through the motions. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right... I just don't want to sound like I'm whining or making a big deal out of nothing. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you lost any weight recently?

Um, I haven't really stepped on a scale recently, so I hope it's okay that I don't have an exact number for you. But... well, like I was saying when I first came in, with barely having an appetite for the last few weeks and just forcing down those few bites after my shifts? I guess because of that, my uniform pants are definitely fitting a little looser than normal. 

I don't think it's anything too drastic, though. I really don't want to make it sound like I'm wasting away or anything like that. Just maybe a few pounds, I guess, since I haven't been eating my normal meals. Is that... does that answer your question? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Would you say the weight loss has been significant enough that others have noticed?

Oh, um, no, I don't think anyone else has really said anything. Like I mentioned when we first started talking, it's really just been these last few weeks where I've barely had an appetite and have just been forcing down those few bites after my shifts. 

Since it hasn't been going on for a super long time, I probably don't look all that different to my family or the guys at work. I really hope I'm not making too much of it... I just figured I should bring it up since, you know, even the foods I usually like are just sitting there on the plate untouched. 

Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for. I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Has this feeling of being down and the loss of appetite been affecting your ability to work or interact with your family?

Well, um... I really want to say no, because I'm still showing up for my shifts and getting the basics done, you know? I don't want you to think I'm slacking off or anything. I'm trying really hard to keep everything normal.

But... well, I guess if I'm being completely honest, it has been a little tough lately. I've made a few documentation mistakes on my logs, and... I actually missed a surveillance cue the other day. It wasn't anything huge, but I did get a formal warning for it. It's just so embarrassing to even admit that, because I've always been really good at my job. It's just... it's starting to affect things in a way it never used to, with this heavy feeling and not eating. 

I hope it's okay that I'm telling you this. I just want to be honest so you can help me. Does that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Have you been thinking a lot about your weight or how you look lately?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I hope it doesn't seem like I'm, you know, obsessed with my appearance or anything like that. I've never really been the type to spend a lot of time in front of the mirror. 

It's really just the clothes fitting a little looser because of the appetite thing, like I mentioned before. I'm definitely not trying to lose weight on purpose or worrying about how I look. I just try to look neat and professional for work, of course. 

I hope that's okay to say. I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right. Is that what you meant?
Have you been feeling guilty after eating?

Oh, um, no. No, definitely not. I hope it doesn't sound like I have some sort of eating problem or anything like that. I really don't. 

Like I said, it's just that the food doesn't sound good, and I'm just forcing it down so I don't pass out at work or something. But when I do manage to eat, I don't feel bad about it afterward. I actually feel a little relieved that I got something in my stomach, you know? 

I really hope I'm explaining this right. I just don't want you to think I'm doing this on purpose or feeling weird about the food itself. Does that make sense? I hope that answers what you were asking.
Has something specific happened recently that you think might be contributing to your loss of appetite?

Well, um... I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining about work, because I know I'm lucky to have my job. I'm usually very adaptable, you know? I always try to be a team player. 

But, I guess... well, this whole thing started about three weeks ago. The casino reorganized our security operations and, um, they changed my assignments around. I mean, it's fine, I'm handling it, I really am. I don't want you to think I can't handle a little change. It's just... I think maybe the stress of the new routine kind of threw me off, and that's when I stopped feeling hungry. 

I hope it doesn't sound like I'm making excuses or blaming the job. I know they have to do what's best for the casino. Is it normal for something like a schedule change to affect your appetite like that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Do you often think about food or your weight when you're not eating?

Um, no, honestly I don't. I really hope I'm not sounding like a broken record, but it just doesn't cross my mind much at all. When I'm not eating, I'm usually just trying to focus on my shift in the surveillance room, making sure I'm doing a good job, you know? 

I definitely don't sit around obsessing over calories or the scale or anything like that. I'd hate for you to think I was hiding some sort of fixation on it. It's really just that food is sort of... an afterthought right now. 

I hope that's an okay answer. I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture of what's going on. Is that helpful?
Would you estimate that you've lost more than 5% of your body weight since your appetite changed?

Um, I don't think it's been that much, honestly. I haven't been weighing myself or anything, so I can't say for sure, but my uniform still fits mostly the same. Maybe just a tiny bit looser, but nothing crazy. 

Like I was saying, I really just came in because for the last few weeks I've barely had an appetite. Even the foods I usually like after a long shift, I just sit there and kind of force down a few bites. It's just not appealing right now. 

I really hope that doesn't sound like I'm letting myself go or not taking care of myself. I'm trying my best to keep my strength up for work. Does that sound like it could be a 5% loss? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right.
Have you been experiencing any pleasure or interest in activities you normally enjoy outside of work?

Well, um... I really hope it doesn't sound like I'm just being lazy or, you know, wasting my free time. I always try to stay active and keep busy when I'm not at the casino. 

But lately... I guess I've just been a little off my routine. I usually really look forward to my morning runs, and I used to play my guitar a lot, or spend time cooking a nice dinner. But recently, I don't know, I keep skipping them. It's not that I don't want to be productive! It's just... they almost feel like chores right now, and I just can't seem to get myself to care about doing them the way I used to. 

I really don't want you to think I'm just giving up on my hobbies or being ungrateful for my time off. I'm sure it's just a phase and I'll bounce back soon. Is it normal to feel that way when your routine changes at work? I hope I'm explaining this okay for you.
Have you noticed any significant change in your weight, such as having to buy smaller clothes?

Um, no, I haven't had to buy any new clothes or anything like that. Like I mentioned before, my uniform still fits pretty much the same. I really hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. 

The main thing, like I was saying, is just that my appetite has been so low lately. For the past few weeks, I just haven't felt like eating. Even when I get home from a long shift and try to make something I normally really enjoy, I just end up staring at it and forcing myself to take a few bites. 

I really don't want it to seem like I'm starving myself on purpose or doing anything reckless. I know how important it is to eat right, especially with my job. I'm really trying my best to keep eating, it's just... hard right now. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question the way you need me to.
Do you find yourself thinking about your body shape or weight when you're not trying to eat or think about food?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I hope it doesn't sound like I'm obsessed with my appearance or anything like that. I'm really not. I'm just a regular guy, you know? 

I don't spend a lot of time analyzing my body shape or worrying about my weight when I'm just going about my day or working my shifts. I try to stay focused on my job and being professional. 

It's really just the eating part that's been a struggle lately, like I was saying. The thought of food just isn't there, but I'm definitely not fixating on how I look in the mirror or trying to lose weight on purpose. I know that wouldn't be healthy. 

I hope that's a good answer for you. Is that what you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of what's going on.
Have you been having any thoughts about harming yourself lately?

Oh, um... no. Definitely not. I really hope you don't think I'm, you know, a danger to myself or anything like that. I would never actually do anything to hurt myself, I promise. I know how serious that is, especially in my line of work. 

It's just... well, sometimes—and I feel a little ashamed even admitting this out loud—I just get so worn out. And I've had these... these passing thoughts that, um, maybe it wouldn't be the absolute worst thing if I just didn't wake up one morning? Just so I didn't have to keep pushing through all of this every single day. 

But I'm really not planning anything, I swear! I think it's just my brain's way of saying I'm exhausted and need a break. I hope I'm not alarming you by saying that, I just want to make sure I'm answering you honestly and being a good patient. Is it okay that I shared that? I really don't want you to worry about me.
How long have you been feeling uninterested in your morning runs and playing guitar?

Um, I guess it's been about... maybe three weeks now? Right around the time the casino did a big reorganization of our security operations. They, um, they changed up my assignments and my schedule a bit. 

I really hope it doesn't sound like I'm complaining about my job or anything. I know I'm lucky to have it, and I always want to be a team player. It's just that since the changes, I've just been feeling a little off my game, I suppose. 

I've been trying to force myself to get back out there for my runs, and I keep telling myself I'll pick up the guitar this weekend, but... I don't know, the energy just hasn't been there. I'm really trying not to let it get the best of me, though. I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline for all this.
How long have you been feeling this heavy, flat feeling that you mentioned earlier?

Um, well, it's actually the exact same timeline as the other stuff I just mentioned. Right around three weeks now. It started right when the casino reorganized our security operations and changed my assignments. 

I hope I don't sound like a broken record, bringing work up again. I really don't want to come across like I'm just whining about my job, because I'm definitely grateful to have it and I know I just need to adapt. It's just... yeah, that's when that heavy sort of feeling really started settling in. 

I'm doing my absolute best to shake it off, though, I promise. I don't want you to think I'm just letting it beat me. I hope that's helpful? I just want to make sure I'm giving you clear answers and being helpful.
Have you been feeling hopeless about your future most of the time over the past few weeks?

Um, hopeless? Oh, no, I wouldn't say hopeless. I mean, I really don't want to sound like I'm giving up or anything like that. I know things will get better, and I'm really trying to stay positive for my family and my team at work. 

It's more just... well, like I was saying before about that heavy feeling? It's just kind of always there lately. Like, most days I'm just carrying this... this flat sort of weight around with me. Even when I'm at home with my wife and kids, or just sitting in the break room with the guys at the casino... I'm there, but it's like I'm not *really* there, if that makes sense? 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad husband or a bad employee. I'm still doing everything I'm supposed to do, I promise. I just... I don't feel quite as present as I usually am. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
How long have you been feeling uninterested in activities you normally enjoy, such as your morning runs and playing guitar?

Oh, um... I think I might have mentioned that a little bit earlier, but I probably wasn't very clear, I'm so sorry about that. But yeah, it's been about three weeks now. It all started right around the time the casino reorganized our security operations and switched up my assignments. 

I really hope I'm not repeating myself too much or wasting your time. Did you need me to go into more detail about that part of it? I just want to make sure I'm answering everything exactly the way you need me to.
How long have you been feeling uninterested in things you usually enjoy?

Um, I think... wait, I think you might have just asked me that one? About the guitar and the running? I'm so sorry if I confused you earlier, I know I tend to ramble sometimes. 

But yeah, it's been about three weeks for that, too. Ever since the work changes started. I really hope I'm not being difficult or making your job harder by not being clear enough the first time. I'm trying my best to give you good answers, I promise. Did I misunderstand what you were asking just now?
